newsitem.title: EGYPT: Gunmen wound two policemen in southern Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen wound two policemen in southern Egypt.

text.p: Gunmen thought to be Islamist militants shot and wounded two policemen on duty in southern Egypt on Sunday, security sources said.
It was the fifth militant operation in the area in the last three days. Eleven people have been killed in the attacks, which mark the most violent episode there for months.

The attack on Sunday took place near the town of Sahel Selim, close to where two police guards were killed on Friday night. The town is in the Nile valley about 320 km (200 miles) south of the capital Cairo.
The sources said a gunfight was under way near the scene as police pursued the gunmen.
Police believe the gunmen belong to the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest militant group fighting to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the conflict broke out in early 1992.
